newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia may postpone bankruptcy law - paper.
newsitem.headline: Croatia may postpone bankruptcy law - paper.

text.p: Croatia may postpone the implementation of the bankruptcy law amid fears that it may push many of the country's over 15,000 insolvent firms into liquidation, a newspaper reported on Tuesday.
The law, passed in May, should have come into force on January 1, 1997 and was supposed to help creditors and suppliers collect their money.
Daily Vjesnik, quoting figures from the central payments bureau (ZAP), said mounting debts in the economy totalled 7.36 billion kuna in September.
There were 15,514 insolvent firms, employing some 150,000 people. Some 90 percent of them are privately owned, Vjesnik said.

Under pressure from various social groups, Croatian authorities said they would put off introduction of value added tax (VAT) for a year, as it would have increased the price of basic consumables which are not taxed now. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
